hints: Look at the M+1 peak first, it is mostly caused by carbon-13 atoms hiding in the molecule, so its size tells you about carbon count.
A ratio of 4 to 91 is about 4.4%, and with about 1.1% contribution per carbon, work out how many carbons J must contain.
Now use the oxidation clue, only a primary alcohol or an aldehyde gives a carboxylic acid with hot acidified dichromate, so match carbon number with functional group.
walkthrough:
**Decode the M+1 to M+ ratio**

Think of the M+1 peak as molecules that are 1 mass unit heavier because they contain one $^{13}\text{C}$ atom instead of $^{12}\text{C}$. Natural abundance of $^{13}\text{C}$ is about 1.1%, so each carbon adds about 1.1% to the height.

$$\text{number of C} \approx \frac{\text{height of M+1}}{\text{height of M+}} \times \frac{100}{1.1}$$

**Calculate the number of carbons in J**

Here the ratio is 4:91, so the percentage is very friendly to calculate.

$$\frac{4}{91} \times 100 \approx 4.4\%$$

Divide by 1.1% per carbon gives about 4 carbons. So J is a $\text{C}_4$ compound.

**Use the oxidation test to find the functional group**

Heating with acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is strong oxidation. Only primary alcohols and aldehydes are oxidised all the way to a carboxylic acid. Ketones resist oxidation and nitriles do not give this reaction.

That leaves a $\text{C}_4$ aldehyde, which is butanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$.

options.A: Butanal is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$ with 4 carbons, matching the 4.4% M+1 ratio. As an aldehyde, $\text{RCHO}$, it is oxidised by hot acidified dichromate to butanoic acid. Both clues fit perfectly.
options.B: Butanone also has 4 carbons so it fits the mass spectrum, but as a ketone it is not oxidised by acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$. Students who only use the carbon count trap often pick this.
options.C: Propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol so it does oxidise to a carboxylic acid (propanoic acid), but it has only 3 carbons. That would give an M+1 ratio of about 3.3%, not 4.4%.
options.D: Propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, contains 3 carbons so the M+1 peak would be too small. It also does not form a carboxylic acid on heating with acidified dichromate under these conditions.
